title: Implementing debounce and throttle from scratch
hook: Search boxes fire input on every keystroke; scroll handlers fire hundreds of times per second. Debounce waits for quiet; throttle caps execution rate — both are classic whiteboard implementations tied to timers and closure state.

blocks.text: **Debounce** delays invoking `fn` until `wait` ms pass without another call — only the last burst runs (search autocomplete). **Throttle** ensures `fn` runs at most once per `wait` ms during continuous events (scroll, resize). Both are **higher-order functions** returning wrapped functions that close over timer IDs and last-run timestamps. **Leading edge** debounce/throttle fires immediately then suppresses; **trailing** waits until window end.

entries.plainDefinition: Reset timer on each call; invoke after quiet period.
Allow at most one call per interval while events stream.
Invoke on first call in window, ignore rest until window resets.
entries.example: Submit button debounce leading — instant first click.

entries.plainDefinition: Invoke after last event in window — default debounce behavior.
entries.example: Search API call after user stops typing.

blocks.text: FAANG interviews ask you to **implement debounce from scratch** without lodash. Production: unthrottled scroll handlers jank the main thread; undebounced search hammers your API. **requestAnimationFrame** throttles paint-aligned work — related but not identical. C# has no built-in debounce — you'd use DispatcherTimer or Reactive Extensions throttle/debounce operators with same semantics.

blocks.title: Interview trap: debounce vs throttle
blocks.body: Debounce: wait for pause (resize end). Throttle: steady sampling during stream (scroll position). Wrong choice = laggy UI or API spam.

snippet.label: Debounce from scratch (trailing)
snippet.explanation: clearTimeout + setTimeout resets quiet window. cancel() prevents fire after unmount. preserve this with apply.

snippet.label: Throttle from scratch (time-since-last-run)
snippet.explanation: Leading immediate when gap elapsed; schedules trailing call for end of window — lodash-style hybrid.

snippet.label: C# Reactive throttle/debounce
snippet.code:
var throttled = Observable
    .FromEventPattern<TextChangedEventArgs>(textBox, nameof(TextBox.TextChanged))
    .Throttle(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(300))
    .Select(_ => textBox.Text)
    .Subscribe(query => SearchAsync(query));
snippet.explanation: Rx Throttle ≈ debounce on event stream. Same semantics, different syntax — know mapping for cross-language interviews.

snippet.label: Failure mode: debounce without cancel on SPA route change
snippet.explanation: Timers survive component lifecycle unless cleared — pair debounce with cancel and abort signal.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Using debounce for scroll position (use throttle or rAF). Forgetting cancel on unmount. Not preserving this/args. Confusing lodash debounce options (leading, trailing, maxWait) in interview without clarifying.

blocks.text: Interview extensions: implement **maxWait** (guarantee fire during long burst), **flush** (invoke pending immediately), and **async debounce** (ignore stale results with incrementing request id). In production measure: debounce 300ms search saves 90% API calls; throttle scroll to rAF for layout reads (getBoundingClientRect batching).

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: May skip final event — add trailing

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot write debounce without lodash. Swap definitions of debounce and throttle. No mention of cancel/flush or stale async responses.

interviewTakeaways: Debounce: reset timer — fire after quiet period (search).
Throttle: cap rate during continuous events (scroll).
Expose cancel() — timers outlive components without cleanup.
60s: Debounce trailing uses setTimeout reset. Throttle uses last-run timestamp. rAF for paint. Rx Throttle in C#. Cancel on unmount; AbortController for stale fetch.
Follow-up: add leading option and maxWait to your debounce.
commonPitfalls: Using debounce where throttle is needed and vice versa.
No cancel on route change causing stray API calls.
Strong answer: write both from scratch, explain leading/trailing, cancel/flush, C# Rx mapping.

jsTsCorrelations.note: debounce<T extends (...args: any[]) => void>(fn: T): T & { cancel(): void } preserves parameter types of wrapped function.
Alternative to throttle for visual work — tied to display refresh not wall clock.
